description.narrative:
OCHA har ansökt till Sida för finansiering om 5 miljoner SEK för att genomföra projektet ”Regional Office for the Caucasus and Central Asia (ROCCA) in support to OCHA operations in Ukraine” under 2014-2015.
Insatsen syftar till att göra det möjligt för OCHA att etablera fältnärvaro i fem nyckelregioner i östra Ukraina (närmare bestämt i städerna Donetsk, Mariupol, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk). Det är de områden som har högst koncentration av internflyktingar. Genom att placera OHCA Humanitarian Advisers dit kommer OCHA att få en starkare position att erbjuda analytisk information som baseras på operationella realiteter, att införa ett systematiskt bevakningsramverk och att underlätta access och effektiv koordination med parterna i konflikten. Insatsen kommer att pågå från december 2014 till juni 2015.

This was an emergency humanitarian intevention agreed upon in December of 2014. The purpose of the intervention was to: - Establish five fild offices in the areas of Ukraine with the highest concentration of IDP's. - To put a monitoring framework in place. - To facilitate access and effective coordination with the parties in the conflict.
The activity period was December 1st 2014-June 30th 2015. Sida's contribution was SEK 5 million.

The project was implemented nearly three years ago so this section is only based on OCHA's final report. According to the reporting, five sub-offices were set up in the east: in Donetsk, Luhansk, Mariupol, Sieverodonetsk and in Kharkiv (relocated to Kramatorsk due to operational priorities). The establishemnt of a monitoring framework started in 2015 but was to be completed when the report was drafted. According to the reporting, access to reliable information on various aspects of the humanitarian situation was limited in June of 2015, which hindered rigorous planning and monitoring of aid delivery. According to the reporting, OCHA's increased field presence strenghtened its capacity to collect information to guide common situational analysis and joint planning. On a regular basis OCHA issued various types of situation updates (maps, bulletins etc.) in order to forge common situational awareness and analysis.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
